description: Stateless application servers. Each replica has a worker pool and a bounded queue. Outgoing links are called in order for matching request types (e.g. reads to the cache, writes to the database). Runs on VMs, containers, Kubernetes (optional autoscaling) or as a serverless function.
modeled: FIFO queue per replica with a size limit and a wait timeout
Worker pool per replica; service time sampled from the configured distribution
Technology behaviour: event loops (Node.js), stop-the-world GC pauses, JIT warm-up of new instances, runtime-specific serverless cold starts
Sequential downstream calls; blocking (thread-per-request) or non-blocking I/O
Autoscaling (when on): utilization-driven replica count with evaluation interval, start-up delay and scale-down stabilization
Serverless (platform): one request per instance, cold starts, concurrency limit and scale-out rate (throttling), idle reclaim
CPU cores (when set): the CPU share of service time needs a core; with fewer cores than workers, work queues for a core
Memory (when set): requests held by a replica use memory; past the limit new requests are refused; memory per req/s adds memory that follows throughput (reported and sized, reclaimable)
notModeled: OOM kills and restarts (memory is a refusal limit instead); concurrent GC CPU overhead
CPU per request that changes with load (one value per request: calibration fits it where load is highest)
Parallel fan-out calls (dependencies are called one after another)
Node/cluster capacity limits for new pods, readiness probe failures
Serverless memory-to-CPU scaling (set CPU directly) and provisioned concurrency

presets.description: Fixed replicas on virtual machines, thread-per-request workers.
presets.name: Generic service (VM)

presets.description: Spring Boot containers with a large blocking thread pool (Tomcat-style).
presets.name: Java/Spring on Docker

presets.description: One event loop per container: every request's CPU work queues for that single thread, while I/O waits don't hold it.
presets.name: Node.js on Docker

presets.description: Go pods behind a Kubernetes Service with a Horizontal Pod Autoscaler.
presets.name: Go service on Kubernetes (HPA)

presets.description: Gunicorn-style worker processes in pods, autoscaled by an HPA.
presets.name: Python service on Kubernetes (HPA)

presets.description: Function-as-a-service: an instance per concurrent request, cold starts when scaling out.
presets.name: Serverless function (Lambda-style)

dotnet.detail: Methods start unoptimised and are recompiled once hot, so a fresh instance is slower at first (factor and duration are illustrative).
dotnet.title: Tiered compilation warm-up

dotnet.detail: Gen0 collections pause managed threads briefly (illustrative).
dotnet.title: GC pauses

go.detail: Requests run as goroutines scheduled across all cores; the concurrent GC's stop-the-world pauses are usually under 100 microseconds.
go.title: Goroutines on every core

java.detail: Spring MVC on Tomcat serves each request on a pool thread (200 by default) that stays busy during downstream calls.
java.title: Thread per request

java.detail: The garbage collector (G1 by default) pauses all application threads for a few milliseconds when the young generation fills up, more often under load (pause and frequency are illustrative).
java.title: Stop-the-world GC pauses

java.detail: A new instance starts with interpreted or lightly optimised code and runs slower until the JIT has compiled the hot paths (factor and duration are illustrative).
java.title: JIT warm-up

nodejs.detail: JavaScript runs on one thread per process: CPU work of every request queues for that one loop (event-loop lag), while I/O waits don't hold it. Add processes per replica (cluster mode) to use more cores.
nodejs.title: Single-threaded event loop

nodejs.detail: V8's scavenger pauses the loop for a couple of milliseconds now and then (illustrative).
nodejs.title: Short GC pauses

php.detail: Each request takes a PHP-FPM child; pm.max_children (5 in the shipped www.conf) caps concurrency and memory is freed when the request ends.
php.title: Process per request (PHP-FPM)

python.detail: Gunicorn-style sync workers handle one request each; each process is held to one core by the GIL (the docs suggest 2 x cores + 1 workers).
python.title: Worker processes

rust.detail: Memory is freed deterministically: no GC pauses and no JIT warm-up.
rust.title: No garbage collector
